findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cron cancellation pass, and the failure repeats every run
findings.body:
The cancellation loop has a single try/catch around all reminders. Each reminder awaits `client.request(...)`, and its DB delete is only queued as a lazy PrismaPromise in `workflowRemindersToDelete`. That array is executed by `Promise.all` only after the loop finishes.

If any SendGrid call throws (transient error, invalid or already-cancelled batch_id), three things go wrong:
1. Every remaining reminder in this run is skipped.
2. None of the queued deletes run, including those whose SendGrid cancel already succeeded.
3. On the next run (15 min later) those already-cancelled batch_ids are POSTed again. SendGrid rejects a second POST for a batch that already has a status, so the loop throws again at the same point.

The result is a persistent failure loop. Every other cancelled reminder in the 1-hour window is never cancelled and its email is sent, which is the bug this PR is meant to fix.

Fix: handle errors per reminder, delete or mark each row right after its cancel succeeds, and treat an "already cancelled" response as success.

findings.title: immediateDelete path cancels at SendGrid but leaves the row (possibly already `cancelled: true`) for the cron to cancel again
findings.body:
With `immediateDelete`, the function POSTs a cancel to SendGrid and returns. It does not delete or update the WorkflowReminder row.

A common sequence leads to a double cancel:
1. A booking is cancelled (handleCancelBooking) or the host uses requestReschedule. Its email reminders get `cancelled: true` and the rows stay.
2. The booker then reschedules. `getOriginalRescheduledBooking` includes CANCELLED bookings, so handleNewBooking calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(id, referenceId, true)` on those same rows, and SendGrid cancels the batch immediately.
3. The rows still have `cancelled: true`, so the cron later POSTs a cancel for the same batch_id. SendGrid rejects it, which triggers the loop-abort problem in scheduleEmailReminders.ts.

Fix: after a successful immediate cancel, delete the row, or at least clear `cancelled` / set `scheduled: false`.

findings.title: Reschedules and workflow/step deletions still cancel immediately, so the 100 pending-cancellation cap can still be exhausted
findings.body:
The PR says cancellations fail once SendGrid has 100 pending `scheduled_sends` cancellations. It fixes this by deferring cancellation to the cron within 1 hour of send time.

However, rescheduling (this line) still passes `immediateDelete = true`. So do workflow deletion (workflows.tsx line 214) and step deletion (workflows.tsx line 521).

Each immediate cancel stays pending in `scheduled_sends` until the original send time, which can be up to 72h away. A handful of reschedules, or deleting one workflow with 100+ scheduled reminders, fills the account-wide quota. After that every cancellation fails, including the cron's deferred ones, and emails go out for cancelled and rescheduled bookings. Rescheduled bookings are explicitly in scope of this fix.

Fix: reschedule should use the deferred `cancelled` flag like cancel does. For workflow/step deletion, avoid the cascade removing rows before the cron runs, for example by detaching or flagging the reminders instead of cancelling immediately.

findings.title: Deferring every cancellation to the 15-minute cron misses reminders that are about to be sent
findings.body:
Cancellation is always deferred by setting `cancelled: true`, even when the reminder's `scheduledDate` is already inside or near the cron's 1-hour window. The cron runs only every 15 minutes, and SendGrid does not guarantee cancellation of a scheduled send less than about 10 minutes before `send_at`.

So if a booking is cancelled or rescheduled roughly 25 minutes or less before a reminder fires, the cancel may happen too late or not at all, and the email is sent. Before this PR the cancellation was attempted immediately.

Fix: cancel immediately when `scheduledDate` is within the cron look-ahead window, and defer only reminders further out.
